Internal helper: stop on infinite values an analysis cannot use

Source: R/checks.R
dot-jst_stop_infinite.Rd

Session 394 (Fix Slate 30; the (S392) infinite-value item, on the lean Jeff okayed: "Yes to everything."). A variable holding Inf or -Inf – what log() of a zero gives, or a division by zero – reached the analyses as a number: jt() stopped on R's "missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed" with no jt(): in front; jaov(), jlm() and jlogistic() on lm.fit()'s "NA/NaN/Inf in 'y'" (jaov() after a Group Descriptives row reading Inf); jcorr() printed r = NaN; jalpha() printed a blank alpha under a warning naming items "NA, NA, NA"; and jplot() drew a histogram without a case its N line counted, under ggplot2's "Removed 1 rows" warning. One stop now, under the Case Processing block (in jplot(), under the N line), naming each variable and its count of infinite values among the cases the analysis uses.

Usage

.jst_stop_infinite(
  data,
  vars,
  data_name = NULL,
  what = "this analysis cannot use"
)

Arguments

data

The cases the analysis uses (a data frame).

vars

Character; the variables to check. A variable that is not stored as double (a factor, text, integers) cannot hold an infinite value and is skipped.

data_name

Character or NULL; the data frame's name.

what

Character(1); the end of the first sentence.

Value

Invisibly NULL when no variable holds an infinite value; otherwise never returns.

Details

jstats does not make the values missing on its own, as it never assumes a blank text cell is missing (Session 340): the stop gives the line that does it in a new variable (voice Rule G's R suffix) and the call run on that variable. A computed term in a formula is different: jstats computed it, and a value that became infinite is set to missing with a note (AUDIT-024, .jst_resolve_formula_transforms()), so it never reaches this stop. Spearman's and Kendall's correlations rank the values and can use them, so jcorr() calls this for Pearson's only.

The lines are given when the data frame's name can be typed, as ruling R19's stop gives its add-it lines (.jst_frame_object_text()); the call, when the user's call is in hand (.jst_caller_call()), each variable swapped for its new one wherever the call names it, bare or in quotes, never in a function's place.
